item.text: {"search_note":"The strongest positive evidence is rhetorical: long-run targets plus a narrow digital-innovation pilot. The stronger empirical evidence points the other way: opacity for major firms, pervasive corruption, property insecurity, and war-driven economic management. No solid 2024 evidence emerged of durable rule-of-law reforms for business, anti-corruption enforcement that constrained insiders, or broad trade/investment liberalization. The main “pro” material was aspirational planning language, not observable institutional change. I did not find credible 2024 evidence of a broad, predictable, pro-competition reform package that would materially improve property rights or investment conditions.","evidence":[{"title":"Executive Order on Russia's development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036","publisher":"President of Russia","date":"2024-05-07","url":"https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986","summary":"Sets long-run targets for investment growth, higher living standards, fair competition, entrepreneurship, and private initiative.
